rows.question: opp cast [[Blood Moon]] while i have all three tron lands out. do i still get my 7 mana from urza's? can i tap tower for 3 colorless or is it just a Mountain now
rows.expected_answer: Tron is off. Blood Moon is a type-changing effect (layer 4, 613.1d) that sets each nonbasic land's subtype to Mountain. Per 305.7, a land whose subtype is set to a basic land type loses its old land types (so it is no longer an Urza's land), loses all abilities from its rules text (the colorless mana ability), and gains only '{T}: Add {R}'. Each Urza's land is a plain Mountain that taps for one red mana; Tower does not produce three because it no longer has that ability and the others no longer have the Urza's subtype. They are still nonbasic (305.8), so Blood Moon keeps affecting them.

No. Each Urza's land is a nonbasic land, so under **Blood Moon** ("Nonbasic lands are Mountains.") it becomes a Mountain. Per the Scryfall ruling, nonbasic lands lose their other land types and abilities and gain "{T}: Add {R}." Tower can't tap for {C}{C}{C}. Each land taps for just {R}, so you get 3 mana total instead of 7.

The type change happens in layer 4 (613.1d), and the lands lose their abilities with it. Even if you read the Tron condition on its own, you no longer control an Urza's Mine, Power-Plant or Tower, because those are land types and the lands are now just Mountains. The lands keep their names, but names don't matter for the check. The Tron abilities check land types, not names. You would only keep the bonus mana if the lands were still Urza's lands when the ability resolved, and they aren't.

rows.question: my goyf has two +1/+1 counters on it and I just giant growthed it. opponent [[Clone]]s it. is their clone a huge goyf too or just a regular one? and does the clone even know how big a goyf should be since the p/t is */*+1
rows.expected_answer: Just a regular Tarmogoyf. A copy acquires only the copiable values of the original (707.2): name, mana cost, types, rules text, printed P/T, etc. Counters, Giant Growth's +3/+3, and other non-copy effects are not copiable values, so the Clone gets none of them. The Clone does copy Tarmogoyf's rules text, and therefore its characteristic-defining ability (707.2a), so the Clone's own P/T is */*+1 computed from card types in graveyards (applied in layer 7a, 613.4a). The copy effect itself is applied in layer 1a (613.2a); your goyf's counters and pump are layer 7c (613.4c) and stay on your goyf only.

outcome.answer:
The Clone is a regular Goyf, not a huge one. It copies only the printed text, so it doesn't copy the two +1/+1 counters or Giant Growth's +3/+3. It does have Tarmogoyf's characteristic-defining ability, so it knows how big to be. Its power is the number of card types among cards in all graveyards, and its toughness is that number plus 1. Your Goyf is then 5 more power and toughness than the Clone, from the 2 counters and the +3/+3.

Rule 707.2 says the copiable values come from the text printed on the object, as modified by other copy effects. It also says "Other effects (including type-changing and text-changing effects), status, counters, and stickers are not copied." The Clone ruling says the same: it copies no counters and no non-copy effects that changed power or toughness.

The */*+1 is part of the copiable values, so the Clone has the ability. Clone's exception-free copy doesn't use 707.9d, which only removes characteristic-defining abilities when the copy effect sets that characteristic itself. Clone does neither, so the ability is copied. Giant Growth only gives +3/+3 until end of turn and isn't copied either.

outcome.answer:

Your real creatures are still 1/1 with no abilities, but they are 1/1 only because they have a Humility effect applied after nothing overrides it. If Opalescence was out first, Humility has the later timestamp, so its 1/1 applies last. Humility is a 1/1 creature, and any other non-Aura enchantment is also 1/1. Opalescence is also a 1/1 creature, because Humility's effect makes it a creature too. Humility is not itself affected by that.

rows.question: quick one: if I have [[Valki, God of Lies]] in hand can I just cast the Tibalt side for 7? and while it's in my library/graveyard does it count as a planeswalker card for stuff like Vraska's Contempt / Kaya's Ghostform?
rows.expected_answer: Yes. Valki // Tibalt is a modal double-faced card: when you cast it you choose which face you're casting before it goes on the stack, and only that face is evaluated (712.11b, 712.11c), so you can cast Tibalt, Cosmic Impostor for {5}{B}{R} straight from your hand. Once chosen, the spell/permanent has only that face's characteristics (712.8f). But anywhere other than the stack or battlefield (hand, library, graveyard, exile) an MDFC has only its front face's characteristics (712.8a), so it is a legendary creature card named Valki, God of Lies there — never a planeswalker card.

outcome.answer: Yes, you can cast the Tibalt side for {5}{B}{R}. Valki is a modal double-faced card, and you choose which face to cast before it goes on the stack (`712.11b`). Only the face you cast is evaluated (`712.11c`). In your hand, library or graveyard it counts only as a creature card, though. Outside the stack and battlefield it has only its front face's characteristics (`712.8a`), so it is never a planeswalker card there. Vraska's Contempt and Kaya's Ghostform both work on permanents. Contempt targets a creature or planeswalker on the battlefield, and Ghostform enchants one. If Tibalt is on the battlefield with his back face up, he has only Tibalt's characteristics (`712.8f`) and is a planeswalker, so both cards can target or enchant him. If Valki is on the battlefield front face up, he is a creature, so both still work, just as a creature.

rows.question: cast Stomp off my bonecrusher giant, it resolved and went to exile. my opp says I can only cast the creature half from exile now, not Stomp again, is that right? also can they counter Stomp with a 'counter target creature spell' effect since the card is a creature?

When an Adventure spell resolves it is exiled instead of going to the graveyard, and you may cast the card from exile — but only as the creature (Bonecrusher Giant), not as Stomp again (715.3d). And no, Stomp can't be hit by 'counter target creature spell': while on the stack as an Adventure the spell has only its alternative characteristics (715.3a, 715.3b), so it is a red instant, not a creature spell. outcome.answer:
Your opponent is right on the first point, and no on the second. After Stomp resolves, you may play the card from exile, but only as the creature. Per 715.3d, "It can't be cast as an Adventure this way." Only another effect that allows you to cast it could let you cast it as an Adventure again.

A 'counter target creature spell' effect can't target Stomp. While a spell is on the stack as an Adventure, per 715.3b it "has only its alternative characteristics." Those are the characteristics of an instant, not a creature. The card's normal creature characteristics are ignored (715.4), so Stomp isn't a creature spell and isn't a legal target.
